**3B.8 Research Note**

Bottom line: the 2024 record is strongly negative. Hasina’s government did not allow peaceful protest and dissent without retaliation; it responded with curfews, internet/text shutdowns, army deployment, arrests, and broad coercive pressure. The closest positive evidence is limited to temporary restoration of internet service after protests were called off, which looks reactive rather than protective.

- [Bangladesh blocks roads and internet, deploys army to curb protests](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-blocks-roads-and-internet-deploys-army-to-curb-protests/2183179/) — Reuters, July 20, 2024. Claim: Reuters reported soldiers in Dhaka, roadblocks, and suspension of internet/text services during the protest crackdown; this is direct evidence of retaliation against peaceful dissent and community mobilization. IDs: `3B.8`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `3B.1`, `2B.4`
- [Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-pm-hasina-blames-opposition-for-violence-curfew-to-remain-3528153) — Reuters, July 22, 2024. Claim: Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence, which reads as selective punishment and a chilling signal to dissenters rather than toleration of protest. IDs: `3B.8`, `3B.3`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`, `2B.6`
- [Bangladesh’s crackdown on protesters left more than 170 dead, U.N. says](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights) — United Nations / OHCHR, July 26, 2024. Claim: The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity; this strongly indicates dissent was met with state violence and a climate of fear, not permitted as peaceful civic activity. IDs: `3B.8`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.9`
- [Bangladesh security forces target unarmed students](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/22/bangladesh-security-forces-target-unarmed-students) — Human Rights Watch, July 22, 2024. Claim: HRW reported security forces targeting unarmed students alongside Awami League-affiliated activists; that is strong evidence that peaceful protest and organization were not protected from retaliation. IDs: `3B.8`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`
- [Bangladesh prime minister Hasina resigns amid mass protests](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/06/bangladesh-prime-minister-hasina-resigns-amid-mass-protests) — Human Rights Watch, August 6, 2024. Claim: HRW described extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, and attacks on protesters during the crackdown; this is direct evidence of retaliation against dissent rather than tolerance of lawful protest. IDs: `3B.8`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.9`
- [Bangladesh: repression, security force abuses discredit elections](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/bangladesh-repression-security-force-abuses-discredit-elections) — Human Rights Watch, January 11, 2024. Claim: HRW reported arrests for criticism and widespread repression before the election, showing that dissent was already being chilled early in 2024, not protected. IDs: `3B.8`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `2B.4`, `2B.5`
- [Bangladesh restores internet as students call off job-quota protests](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-restores-internet-as-students-call-off-jobquota-protests-3540555) — Reuters, July 29, 2024. Claim: Internet service was restored only after protesters called off the movement and conditions were said to be normalizing; this is the closest weak counterevidence, but it shows de-escalation after coercive disruption, not a willingness to permit protest without retaliation. IDs: `3B.8`, `3B.5`, `3B.6`
- [Bangladesh will not let in any more Rohingya refugees - minister](https://theprint.in/world/bangladesh-will-not-let-in-any-more-rohingya-refugees-minister/1958020/) — Reuters, February 7, 2024. Claim: Bangladesh framed refusal to admit additional Rohingya as a security necessity; this is a limited positive only in the sense of defensive border control, but it does not show openness to dissent or community organization inside Bangladesh. IDs: `3B.8`, `2B.3`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Hasina’s government genuinely tolerated peaceful protest, dissent, or independent community organization without retaliation.
- I also did not find reliable evidence of a durable non-retaliatory framework such as protected protest permits, noninterference with civil society, or restraint in surveillance and selective punishment.
- The best available counterevidence is just a post-crackdown internet restoration after protests were called off, which is too weak to offset the broader repression record.
